 Management attributed a 55% increase in segment net operating income to strengthening trends across the multifamily, office, and hotel portfolios, with the multifamily segment specifically seeing a 169% year-over-year NOI increase. 
 The recovery in the Bay Area multifamily market is being driven by growth in AI-related employment and investment, leading to rent growth at 25-year highs and vacancy in San Francisco is at a 25-year low. 
 Operational performance at the Sacramento hotel asset improved significantly following the completion of guest room and public space renovations, resulting in a 234% year-over-year increase in NOI. 
 Strategic focus remains on closing the gap between the current share price and the portfolio's intrinsic value through targeted asset sales and the redemption of approximately $398.9 million of preferred stock. 
 The company has shifted its capital structure to reduce corporate debt to $27.1 million, with no maturities until 2035, by retiring its recourse credit facility and selling its lending business. 
 Management is prioritizing liquidity and balance sheet strength over reinvesting in underperforming assets, as evidenced by the decision not to commit additional capital to the Oakland office property following its mortgage maturity. 
 Growth Initiatives and Market Capture 
 Management anticipates a multi-year timeline to capture the 17% mark-to-market opportunity in the Bay Area multifamily portfolio as existing leases roll to current asking rates. 
 Future supply growth in the San Francisco and Oakland markets is expected to remain very low for the foreseeable future due to elevated construction costs, supporting sustained occupancy and rent levels. 
 The company is evaluating an accretive opportunity to add 8 new guest rooms at the Sacramento hotel by converting underutilized space, supported by group bookings for 2027 that are already up more than 20%. 
 Predevelopment is underway for 50 additional units at the 701 South Hudson multifamily asset in Los Angeles, with management anticipating the option to start construction next year. 
 Ongoing strategic priorities include the refinancing of mortgages on the hotel asset and two Bay Area multifamily properties to potentially increase loan balances and reduce borrowing spreads. 
 Structural Adjustments and Risk Factors 
 The company recognized $8 million in impairment charges during the third quarter related to office properties in Austin and San Francisco. 
 Management elected not to refinance the nonrecourse mortgage on the Oakland office property, resulting in a $1.6 million negative impact on core FFO due to a stepped-up interest rate accrual. 
 The Lending segment was fully divested in the first quarter of 2026 as part of the broader strategy to simplify the business and strengthen the balance sheet. 
 A significant portion of the company's preferred stock was redeemed in exchange for common stock to reduce dividend obligations and improve funds from operations.

 Q&A Session Insights 
 Asset sales pipeline and current market liquidity dynamics 
 Management is currently marketing several office and residential assets but noted a wide bid-ask spread in the office market due to rising 10-year yields. 
 The primary driver for these sales is to generate liquidity to effectively manage preferred stock redemptions rather than waiting for perfect market conditions. 
 Timeline for capturing 17% multifamily rent mark-to-market gap 
 The 17% gap between in-place and asking rents in the Bay Area has widened because market rents have grown faster than the company can roll existing leases. 
 Management expects it will take approximately a couple of years to fully transition the two primary Bay Area assets to current market rent levels.
